math_steps.note: Pulsing volume rate is the difference between the two acoustic frequencies
math_steps.code:
// 1. Classical acoustic beat frequency and carrier pitch
val beatFreq = abs(f1 - f2)
val carrierFreq = (f1 + f2) / 2f
val beatPeriodSec = if (beatFreq > 0.05f) 1.0f / beatFreq else Float.POSITIVE_INFINITY
math_steps.sub_desc: Computes apparent carrier pitch and rhythmic volume thrum period.

math_steps.note: Trigonometric product identity reveals a slowly breathing amplitude envelope
math_steps.code:
// 2. Wave superposition and modulated envelope
val envelopeAmp = 2f * amp1 * abs(cos(PI.toFloat() * (f1 - f2) * simTime))
val carrierOsc = sin(2 * PI.toFloat() * carrierFreq * simTime)
val yCombined = envelopeAmp * carrierOsc

mystery.en: Why do two slightly out-of-tune notes produce a pulsating rhythm?

en.title: Acoustic Beats & Wave Interference
en.teaser: When two close sound waves overlap, constructive and destructive interference create rhythmic volume beats.

en.hook: Why does playing two notes just two hertz apart make the sound wobble with a rhythmic pulsing beat?
en.math: By trigonometric superposition, two nearby frequencies fuse into a carrier tone modulated by a slow amplitude envelope oscillating at the difference frequency f1 minus f2.
en.question: Can we simulate acoustic beats and interference envelopes live in Kotlin Multiplatform?
en.code_tip: We calculate the exact beat period, synthesize dual audio waveforms, and render real-time phasor interference on Canvas.
en.payoff: Acoustic beat interference and envelope modulation running live in Kotlin.
